problem_statement: Temitayo-spec/Raft-Landing-Page (RAFT) is a polished Next.js 13 App Router single-page marketing site for a generic neobank, built from styled-components section modules (Header, HeroSection, Featured, OffersSection, FinancialFreedom, FinancialFuture, IntroSection, JoinSection, FAQ, Footer) that each read their copy from a co-located constants.ts, plus a GSAP Preloader that spells out the wordmark and a framer-motion MaskText reveal system. The current site is a coherent but entirely generic banking demo (hero 'Building the future of banking', 'RAFT's Next-Gen Cards', 'Your Financial Freedom / Financial Future', a canned demo-filler FAQ, 'Raft Corp, LLC' footer). Rework RAFT into a coherent launch site for a fictional brand and product: Kestrel, a members-owned spending card and studio account for independent makers and small workshops. The centrepiece of this task is a real MEMBERSHIP PRICING section, 'Pick a bench plan', added as a new styled-components module between the benefit sections and the closing content: three plan cards (Solo bench, Shared workshop, Makers union) in a responsive grid, with a Monthly/Yearly billing toggle. The billing cycle is shared through a small context so that flipping the toggle updates BOTH each card's headline price (per-month vs per-year) AND a plain-language billing readout ('Billing: Monthly - pay as you go' vs 'Billing: Yearly - two months on us'), and the same readout echoes on the offers section and in the footer account row. Keep the Next.js/styled-components architecture, the section module boundaries and constants-driven copy pattern, the MaskText/Preloader motion system, the responsive desktop/tablet/mobile behaviour, and the existing local assets. Do not turn the page into a dashboard or a multi-page app, and do not leave leftover RAFT banking copy behind a rebranded hero.
required_content: The wordmark, page title, and hero rebrand from RAFT banking to Kestrel, a members card for makers, instead of 'Building the future of banking'.

A membership pricing section 'Pick a bench plan' presents three plan cards (Solo bench, Shared workshop as the popular plan, Makers union) in a responsive grid with plan names, prices, taglines, feature lists, and a Choose button per card.

A Monthly/Yearly billing toggle drives the section: clicking Yearly updates every plan card's headline price to its per-year figure (e.g. Shared workshop shows £290/yr) and switches the billing readout to 'Billing: Yearly - two months on us'; clicking Monthly returns the per-month figures and the 'pay as you go' readout. The toggle click must actually re-render the prices and readout, not leave them stale.
The shared billing readout echoes on more than one surface: it appears in the pricing section, on the offers section, and in the footer account row, so the whole page reflects one billing cycle.

The benefit sections, statistics, testimonials, and FAQ replace the generic 'Financial Freedom / Financial Future' and canned demo-filler copy with maker/workshop framing while keeping the same module structure; the footer is rebranded to the Kestrel Makers Union rather than 'Raft Corp, LLC'.

The Next.js section modules, constants-driven copy pattern, styled-components layout, MaskText/Preloader motion, local card/avatar/banner assets, and the single-page route remain intact and reachable.

Desktop, tablet, and 390px mobile states keep the polished layout with no broken sections, missing imagery, or horizontal overflow; the plan grid wraps to a single column on mobile rather than forcing a fixed-width row that overflows the viewport.
design_constraints: Preserve RAFT's design language: near-black background, white text, emerald accent, large confident MaskText headings, rounded cards, and the GSAP preloader wordmark. The pricing cards must stay legible (light text on the dark cards) and laid out as separated, non-overlapping cards.

Do not change the framework, the section module boundaries, or the constants.ts-per-section copy convention; the pricing section and billing control should be new styled-components modules that fit the existing architecture.
Keep using the existing local assets under public/images and public/svgs; do not add external stock imagery or remote fonts.
The result must remain a single-page product marketing site, not a dashboard, blog, or multi-page app.
Motion, responsive breakpoints, and the mobile burger nav should keep working; the plan grid and billing readout must stay readable at 390px with no horizontal overflow.
state_constraints: desktop_initial captures the full-width home above the fold: the Kestrel wordmark and nav, the hero headline, and the intro paragraph.
tablet_initial and mobile_initial capture the same home at 834px and 390px, where the burger nav and stacked hero must stay clean with no horizontal overflow.
desktop_offers scrolls to the 'everything a bench needs' offers grid, where the shared billing readout echoes.
desktop_freedom_banner and desktop_future_cards scroll to the fair-terms benefit section and the run-the-studio statistics band.
desktop_plans_default scrolls to the 'Pick a bench plan' membership pricing section with its three plan cards and the Monthly/Yearly toggle in its default (Monthly) state.
desktop_plans_yearly clicks the Yearly toggle: the plan prices switch to their per-year figures and the billing readout reads 'two months on us'.
desktop_plans_monthly_back clicks Yearly then Monthly to confirm the toggle round-trips back to the per-month figures and 'pay as you go' readout.
mobile_plans_yearly repeats the Yearly toggle at 390px, where the plan grid must wrap to a single column with no horizontal overflow.
desktop_intro_cards and desktop_faq_footer scroll to the Kestrel Workshop Card feature and the questions-from-the-bench FAQ plus the rebranded footer, where the billing readout echoes again.

Source inspection confirms the site is a Next.js 13 App Router app whose sections read copy from co-located constants.ts files, so the pricing section is a natural, architecture-preserving addition rather than a rewrite.

change_completion: The 'Pick a bench plan' membership pricing section renders three plan cards with names, prices, taglines, features, and Choose buttons.
The Monthly/Yearly billing toggle updates both the plan prices and the billing readout live on click, and the readout echoes on the offers section and in the footer.
Generic RAFT banking copy (future of banking, Financial Freedom, Financial Future, Happy RAFT User, Raft Corp, and the canned demo-filler answers) no longer appears on the captured page.
Existing local card/avatar/banner assets stay integrated and purposeful.
design_consistency: The pricing section preserves RAFT's dark emerald-accent identity, MaskText headings, and rounded cards, with legible text and separated, non-overlapping plan cards.
The section module boundaries and constants-driven copy convention are preserved.
The result remains a single-page product marketing site.
regression: The Next.js single-page app still builds and serves; every section and the footer remain reachable on one scroll.
The rebranded Kestrel shell (wordmark, hero, nav) and the plan grid persist across the captured states.
responsive: 390px mobile and 834px tablet states have no horizontal overflow; the plan grid wraps to a single column instead of a fixed-width row.
Headings, plan cards, the billing toggle, and the footer wrap cleanly on mobile.

author_notes: Repo-grounded Next.js 13 App Router + styled-components modify task on the RAFT single-page fintech landing, rebranded to 'Kestrel' (a fictional members card for makers). The native marketing lever is a real membership PRICING section, 'Pick a bench plan', with a Monthly/Yearly billing toggle whose shared context drives both the plan prices and a billing readout that echoes on the pricing, offers, and footer surfaces. The task tests four orthogonal things: (D6) the plan grid must wrap on mobile rather than forcing a fixed-width row that overflows 390px; (D3) the plan cards must render as separated, legible cards rather than an overlapping, dark-on-dark collapse; (D2) the shared billing readout must actually appear on all three surfaces; and (D4) the billing toggle must re-render the prices and readout on click rather than freezing them. INFRA (identical across reference/baseline/bad, not task content): the remote SF Pro Display @import in globals.css is replaced with a local system font stack for offline deterministic capture, the Header nav container is rendered as a semantic <nav>, and a BillingProvider context wraps the page. Local card/avatar/banner assets (lola_card.png, orange_card.png, companies.png and the feature illustrations) stay integrated.

metadata.selected_repo_reason: Next.js 13 App Router + styled-components single-page marketing site with clear section-module boundaries, constants-driven copy, and a GSAP preloader wordmark; implementation_continuity modify that rebrands RAFT into Kestrel and adds a native membership pricing section with a Monthly/Yearly billing toggle while preserving the repo architecture, motion, and local assets.
